name: Brno
tagline: Moravia's underrated capital, a lively university city pairing a hilltop fortress and mummified crypt with one of the 20th century's most influential houses.
highlight: Standing in Villa Tugendhat's open-plan living space, realising an entire century of modernist architecture traces back to this single 1930 house.
shortDescription: Moravia's underrated capital, home to Špilberk Castle, the mummified Capuchin Crypt and the UNESCO-listed modernist Villa Tugendhat.
metaDescription: A Brno travel guide: Špilberk Castle, the Capuchin Crypt, Villa Tugendhat, Freedom Square, food and how to plan a visit to Moravia's capital.
knownFor: Špilberk Castle, Villa Tugendhat, the Capuchin Crypt
budget: Kč1,800–3,500 per day, budget to mid-range

image.alt: Špilberk Castle overlooking Brno

intro: Brno is the Czech Republic's second city and Moravia's capital, a lively university town that most Prague-focused visitors skip entirely, to their own loss.
Its sights range from a hilltop fortress and a mummified monastic crypt to one of the most influential private houses of the 20th century, the UNESCO-listed Villa Tugendhat.
It's also South Moravia's natural gateway, well placed for day trips into the region's wine country and smaller historic towns.

whyVisit.intro: Brno's case rests on an unusually varied set of sights for a city that receives a fraction of Prague's visitors.

points.title: Villa Tugendhat is a landmark of modern architecture
points.text: A UNESCO-listed 1930 house that helped define modernism worldwide.

points.title: The Capuchin Crypt is a singular, startling sight
points.text: Naturally mummified monks and nobles, preserved by the crypt's own ventilation system.

points.title: Špilberk Castle is a real hilltop fortress
points.text: Centuries as both a stronghold and a notorious political prison.

points.title: It's a lively, youthful city
points.text: A large student population keeps Brno's bars, cafés and nightlife buzzing.

points.title: It works well as a Moravia base
points.text: Close to Telč, Lednice-Valtice and the wider South Moravian wine country.

attractionsIntro: Brno's essential sights are more varied than its low profile among visitors would suggest.

attractions.name: Špilberk Castle

image.alt: Špilberk Castle above Brno

attractions.text: A hilltop fortress with a dark history as one of the Habsburg Empire's most feared political prisons.
attractions.tip: Walk the castle walls for one of the best panoramic views over the city.

attractions.name: Cathedral of St Peter and Paul (Petrov)

image.file: File:Brno Cathedral St. Peter and Paul-03.jpg
image.alt: The Cathedral of St Peter and Paul on Petrov Hill in Brno

attractions.text: Brno's defining skyline landmark, its twin neo-Gothic spires visible across the city.
attractions.tip: Listen for the noon bells, which famously ring an hour 'early' to commemorate a local legend.

attractions.name: Villa Tugendhat

image.alt: Villa Tugendhat, a UNESCO-listed modernist house in Brno

attractions.text: One of the most influential private houses of the 20th century, designed by Ludwig Mies van der Rohe in 1930.
attractions.tip: Book the tour weeks ahead — timed entry slots are limited and sell out.

attractions.name: Freedom Square (náměstí Svobody)

image.alt: Freedom Square in central Brno

attractions.text: The city's social heart, a triangular square ringed by Renaissance and Art Nouveau facades.
attractions.tip: Check for one of the square's regular markets or events during your visit.

attractions.name: The Capuchin Crypt

image.alt: The Capuchin Crypt in Brno

attractions.text: A startling sight, monks and local nobles naturally mummified by the crypt's own ventilation system.
attractions.tip: A small, quick visit — allow 20 to 30 minutes.

attractions.name: Brno's Astronomical Clock

image.alt: Brno's black granite Astronomical Clock

attractions.text: A striking modern black granite obelisk on Freedom Square, releasing a glass marble each day at noon.
attractions.tip: Arrive at noon and watch the crowd scramble to catch the falling marble.

attractions.name: The view from Špilberk's walls

image.alt: The view over Brno from Špilberk Castle's walls

attractions.text: One of the city's best viewpoints, taking in Petrov's spires and the rooftops below.
attractions.tip: A lovely spot for sunset, with the cathedral lit up as the light fades.

thingsToDoIntro: Brno rewards a full day or two, mixing fortress history with modernist architecture and a lively café scene.

thingsToDo.title: Tour Špilberk Castle's casemates

image.alt: The casemates of Špilberk Castle in Brno

thingsToDo.text: A fascinating, slightly chilling tour through the fortress's former prison cells.
thingsToDo.tip: Combine with the castle museum for the fuller history of the site.

thingsToDo.title: Climb Petrov Cathedral's towers

image.alt: The towers of Petrov Cathedral in Brno

thingsToDo.text: A rewarding climb, one of the best views over Brno's rooftops and surrounding hills.
thingsToDo.tip: Check the tower's separate opening hours before making the trip up Petrov Hill.

thingsToDo.title: Visit the Capuchin Crypt

image.alt: The mummified remains in the Capuchin Crypt in Brno

thingsToDo.text: A memorable, if slightly eerie, half-hour taking in the crypt's naturally preserved remains.
thingsToDo.tip: Treat it with the same quiet respect as the Sedlec Ossuary — this is a real burial site.

thingsToDo.title: Tour Villa Tugendhat

image.alt: The interior of Villa Tugendhat in Brno

thingsToDo.text: An essential visit for anyone interested in architecture, walking through a house that shaped modernism worldwide.
thingsToDo.tip: Book the 'basic' tour first if slots for the 'extended' version aren't available — both cover the key rooms.

thingsToDo.title: Watch the Astronomical Clock's noon marble

image.alt: Crowds at Brno's Astronomical Clock at noon

thingsToDo.text: A fun, low-key local tradition, a small crowd gathering to catch the clock's daily glass marble.
thingsToDo.tip: Arrive a few minutes before noon to get a good spot.

thingsToDo.title: Wander Freedom Square and its cafés

image.alt: Cafés on Freedom Square in Brno

thingsToDo.text: A relaxed way to spend an afternoon, taking in the square's mix of historic and modern architecture.
thingsToDo.tip: Brno's café culture rivals Prague's, with noticeably fewer tourists competing for a table.

foodIntro: Brno's food reflects its Moravian setting, with local wine standing in for Bohemia's beer-first culture.

foods.name: Svíčková (marinated beef in cream sauce)

image.alt: Svíčková, marinated beef in cream sauce with bread dumplings

foods.text: A reliable classic, found at traditional restaurants throughout the city.
foods.whereToTry: Traditional restaurants around Freedom Square and the old town.

foods.name: Guláš with dumplings

image.alt: Czech goulash served with bread dumplings

foods.text: A warming, filling classic, common on menus throughout the city.

foods.name: Moravian wine

image.file: File:Blatnice pod Svatým Antonínkem, wine cellars 01.jpg
image.alt: Traditional Moravian wine cellars

foods.text: A defining part of Brno's identity as Moravia's capital, with excellent regional wine on nearly every wine bar's list.
foods.whereToTry: Wine bars throughout the city centre.

foods.name: Starobrno beer

image.alt: A glass of Starobrno beer, brewed in Brno

foods.text: The city's own brewery, a solid Moravian alternative to Bohemia's more famous pilsners.
foods.whereToTry: Pubs and beer halls throughout central Brno.

foods.name: Smažený sýr (fried cheese)

image.file: File:Smažený sýr s tatarskou omáčkou a brambory.jpg
image.alt: Smažený sýr, breaded fried cheese with tartar sauce and potatoes

foods.text: A satisfying, inexpensive pub classic, just as popular here as in Bohemia.

foods.name: Koláče (fruit-filled pastries)

image.alt: Traditional koláče pastries filled with fruit

foods.text: A homely sweet treat, found at bakeries and cafés across the city.
foods.whereToTry: Bakeries and cafés throughout central Brno.

accommodation.intro: Brno offers noticeably better value than Prague, with everything of interest within easy reach of the centre.

areas.text: The most convenient base, close to restaurants, bars and the main sights.

areas.text: A short walk uphill from the old town centre.

gettingThere.intro: Brno is well connected to both Prague and Vienna, making it an easy addition to a wider Central Europe trip.

options.text: Fast and frequent, taking about 2.5 hours.
options.detail: Direct high-speed services run throughout the day.
RegioJet and FlixBus both run frequent services, similar in journey time to the train.
Takes under two hours, making Brno an easy Central Europe add-on.

gettingAround.intro: Brno's compact centre is easily walkable, with trams covering the rest of the city well.

options.text: The best way to see the old town's main sights.
options.detail: Petrov, Freedom Square and the crypt all sit within a comfortable walk of each other.

options.text: Useful for reaching Špilberk Castle or Villa Tugendhat.
options.detail: A frequent, easy-to-use network covering the wider city.

options.text: Useful late at night or for luggage.
options.detail: Widely available and inexpensive compared to Prague.

bestTime.headline: May, June and September for pleasant weather and a lively city
bestTime.summary: Brno is a year-round city destination, with its university calendar shaping the atmosphere as much as the weather.

seasons.text: Mild, comfortable weather with the city at its liveliest before summer break.
Warm and pleasant, though quieter with students away for the break.
Comfortable weather with the university term back in full swing.
Cold but atmospheric, with a good Christmas market on Freedom Square.

bestTime.avoid: Nothing strongly — Brno works well as a year-round city break.

itinerary.title: Two days in Brno
itinerary.intro: Built around the old town's historic sights and Villa Tugendhat's modernist architecture.

days.title: Špilberk and the old town
days.afternoon: Petrov Cathedral and the Capuchin Crypt.
days.evening: Dinner and drinks around Freedom Square.

days.title: Villa Tugendhat
days.summary: A slower day centred on modernist architecture.
days.afternoon: Wander Freedom Square's cafés and shops.
days.evening: A final dinner in the old town.

tipsIntro: Practical notes that make a Brno visit noticeably smoother.
tips: Book Villa Tugendhat's tour weeks ahead — it does sell out.
Check Petrov Cathedral's tower hours separately from the church itself.
Treat the Capuchin Crypt with the same quiet respect as any burial site.
Arrive at Freedom Square just before noon to catch the Astronomical Clock's marble.
Expect noticeably better prices than Prague for food, drink and accommodation.
Use Brno as a base for day trips to Telč or the Moravian wine country.

faq.a: Yes — it's a lively, underrated city with an unusually varied set of sights for its size.

faq.q: How do you get from Prague to Brno?
faq.a: Easiest by direct train or bus, both taking around 2.5 hours.

faq.q: Is Villa Tugendhat worth the visit?
faq.a: Yes — it's a genuine landmark of 20th-century architecture, and the tour is well worth booking ahead.

faq.q: How many days do you need in Brno?
faq.a: One to two days covers the main sights, with a second day allowing a more relaxed pace.
Yes — accommodation, food and drink all tend to run noticeably cheaper than in the capital.

faq.q: Can you day-trip from Brno into Moravian wine country?
faq.a: Yes, easily — Lednice-Valtice and other South Moravian wine villages are both within easy reach.
